thread:
Marta: quick evening scan before I sign off. Not an incident, but a few recurring noisy signals and one degraded path to watch. TL;DR: kv-cache TTL jitter in eu-west, encoder pool backpressure on long sequences, and short broker ingress spikes during a deploy. Leaving a checklist below.

Marta: Current watchlist (non-critical):
- kv-cache: intermittent TTL variance for short sessions (<=128 tokens) in eu-west; shows slight auth latency bumps and a handful of signature-fail log lines. Seen ~3 times in last 6h. No customer reports.
- encoder-pool: queue depth spikes when seq_len >2048; observed p50->p95 widening on a subset of g4dn-like nodes.
- broker-ingest: brief 30-90s bursts of 502/503 during earlier deploy window. Appears to be upstream churn (ingress proxy) rather than runtime model failures.

Marta: Actions I took: restarted encoder pool service on eu-west-2a (rolled back the canary), bumped encoder pool max_workers +2 on affected pool, and increased kv TTL smoothing window to 60s for eu-west. Did not silence alerts; want to monitor behavior for a few cycles.

Marta: Overnight checklist for whoever is covering:
1) Dashboards: Observability > Oncall > QuickScan. Check kv_cache_ttl_jitter, encoder_queue_depth, broker_upstream_5xx_rate.
2) If kv TTL jitter reappears, toggle feature.kv_ttl_smoothing for eu-west via console (set back to 30s if it overshoots) and observe 15m.
3) If encoder queue depth >75% for >5m, scale pool by +1 node and file a runtime ticket for slow kernel investigation.
4) If broker 5xx bursts return, revert nginx upstreams one version in eu-west; if that stabilizes, schedule a staging repro tomorrow.

Marta: Useful commands:
```
# quick health
curl -s https://observability.internal/api/health | jq '.components.kv_cache.eu-west, .components.encoder_pool.eu-west, .components.broker_ingest.eu-west'

# tail recent errors
gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=\"redwood-eu-west\" AND severity>=ERROR" --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod --format="json" | jq '.[].textPayload' | sed -n '1,120p'
```

Alex: quick q 0h: when you say "TTL smoothing" is that the window in seconds or an amplification factor? don't want to accidentally tank hit ratio.

Marta: Alex  it's the smoothing window in seconds. default 30s, I set 60s for eu-west temporarily. no eviction policy changes.

Priya: saw the broker bursts as well, logged noise on the observability board. propose a runbook note: label short 502 bursts during deploys as deploy-noise if <2m and model_error_rate==0. Want me to add?

Marta: yes please add it under Oncall Runbooks -> NonCritical Noisy Alerts. Condition: if 5xx spike <2m AND model_error_rate == 0 then mark deploy-noise.

Jon: I'll cover overnight. I'll watch encoder pool and scale if queue depth hits 80% for >3m. Marta, did you capture the node id for the restarted pool? want to correlate.

Marta: node id eu-west-2a-node-17. I annotated the event in Observability -> Events -> 2026-03-17-eu-restart.

eng-oncall-bot: Reminder: @Jon is primary for 2026-03-17 22:00 -> 2026-03-18 06:00 UTC. Escalation: ping @platform-sre.

Jon: taking over now. I'll monitor autoscaler oscillation after my manual bump; if it overshoots repeatedly I'll mute noisy scaling alerts and file a follow-up.

Alex: one more ask 0h can someone drop the kv-cache TTL graph link? I'm on mobile.

Priya: link: https://observability.internal/dashboards/kv-cache-ttl-jitter?cluster=eu-west (short link, mobile-friendly).

Marta: thanks everyone. If anything looks user-facing escalate immediately, otherwise put notes in the shift doc. :white_check_mark:

Jon: noted, taking over. will ping if anything changes.

Marta: night!

Jon: night :wave:
